paragraphs: Rabbi Yehudah ben Lakish. (A tanna of a baraita.)

In [Kohelet Rabbah 1:15](https://www.sefaria.org/Kohelet_Rabbah.1.15.2) we find Yehudah ben Lakish teaching in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Gamliel. In the Sifra, Acharei, at the printed locator קלא, the attribution is given as “רש״בג in the name of רש״בל.” Hyman regards this as an error: he proposes that it should read “R' Yehudah ben Lakish says in the name of רש״בג,” citing Yalkut Joshua, remez 23, in support.[^1][^2]

He is also mentioned in baraitot: Shabbat 43; Yoma 53b and 85; Chagigah 9; and in Yerushalmi Sanhedrin, chapter 1, halakhah 1; Mekhilta, Yitro, Parashat BaChodesh, chapter 1; and Tosefta Sotah, chapter 7.[^3]

notes.text: Hyman writes the full רבי in his heading, so Rabbi is retained there. The checked “Midrash Rabbah -- TE” text of Kohelet Rabbah 1:15:2 explicitly says Yehudah ben Lakish in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Gamliel. This supports that full title at this occurrence only. The matching Venice 1545 digital Sifra passage, Acharei Mot, Section 8:7, reads “R' Shimon ben Gamliel says in the name of R' Shimon ben Lakish.” Its abbreviated titles remain R'. Hyman’s printed locator קלא and quoted initials רש״בג and רש״בל are preserved in the translation; the matching digital passage does not establish the original edition’s page or section numbering.

The checked digital Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 23:6 has the opposite direction: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says in the name of R' Yehudah ben Lakish. It does not verify Hyman’s proposed attribution as written. The checked Sifra likewise has Shimon ben Gamliel reporting in the other man’s name, but calls that man Shimon ben Lakish; the Yalkut calls him Yehudah ben Lakish. Thus neither supplied passage establishes the direction of Hyman’s proposed replacement. His argument is translated as his proposed correction, not adopted as an established critical text. Collation of his precise printed editions remains open; no emendation or biographical relationship is admitted here. The title Rabbi in the Kohelet text and Rabban in the Yalkut are each recorded as their own version’s wording.

The original semicolon-like marks after Shabbat מג and Chagigah ט do not establish an amud; those folios remain 43 and 9. The colon after Yoma נג gives 53b; the following פה is treated as a second Yoma folio, 85, without an amud marker. These remaining citations were not independently checked. No historical Sifra page numbering is converted into a guessed modern section.
